objective: Rank keyword candidates extracted from an existing corpus of page JSON documents using interpretable corpus and structure signals.

document_prevalence.description: Fraction of retained documents containing the candidate after consolidation.

heading_presence.description: Normalized frequency of candidate appearance in headings across retained documents.

title_presence.description: Normalized frequency of candidate appearance in titles or descriptions.

phrase_quality.description: Rewards clean multi-word phrases, meaningful noun phrases, and natural surface forms.

entity_bonus.description: Bonus when the candidate is a validated named entity or domain-lexicon match.

semantic_relevance.description: Semantic similarity to the topic embedding or topic anchor phrase. Optional if embeddings are unavailable.

method_agreement.description: Bonus when multiple extraction methods independently surface the same candidate.

redundancy_penalty.description: Penalizes candidates that are near-duplicates of stronger canonical phrases.

junk_penalty.description: Penalizes platform text, UI phrases, or known boilerplate.

genericity_penalty.description: Optional penalty for very broad low-information phrases such as 'dog' or 'breed'.

primary_topic_term.notes: Should be clearly tied to the topic and appear across multiple retained sources.

core_entity.notes: Allows lower prevalence when the entity is clearly topic-relevant and repeated in strong sources.

supporting_phrase.notes: Descriptive or functional phrase that adds topic context.

subtopic.notes: Repeated conceptual area supported by headings and/or body clusters.

heading_candidate.notes: Best used as an H2/H3 idea rather than inline keyword guidance.

question_phrase.notes: Derived from interrogative headings or repeated question patterns.

ignore_noise.notes: Known junk, platform text, blocked-page text, or low-information phrases.

confidence.high: 8+ retained documents with low noise and low duplication
confidence.low: fewer than 5 retained documents or heavy noise / duplication
